params.body:
## The bidding card reads at a glance

The card in the bidding offer (`livewire/bidding-offer-browser.blade.php`) put its most useful fact last and in code. The end date sat under a spaced-capital "EINDDATUM" label in a box with decorative stripes, and the days left were a bare number in a chip with a clock ("6"). That number could just as well be read as six bids. The kind of car stood above the facts in spaced capitals joined by a middot, the year was said twice (title and first registration), and the seller's logo was a 52px bordered box.

What the card says now, with the same information:

- **The deadline is the answer of the card.** "Nog 6 dagen" with "tot en met 07/10/2026" beside it; on the end day "Laatste dag" with "bieden kan tot middernacht" (bids are accepted through the whole end day, R B1-3.1). Only the last day is amber; before, the chip turned amber at two days or less. The count is the calendar days of `ExportVehicle::windowHint`, so on every day before the end day it is the same number the old chip showed (`daysRemaining`); on the end day the chip said "1" and the card now says "Laatste dag".
- **The "6" chip meant days**, not bids: `ExportVehicle::daysRemaining()`, the days left with the end day counted. The active card has never shown a bid count (bids are sealed), and still does not.
- **Title is make and model.** The year is said once, in the first registration. The construction year still shows when there is no registration date or when it is another year than the registration, so no fact is lost.
- **Seller:** a small logo (24px high) inline with the name, normal weight.
- **Facts on one quiet wrapping line**, an icon per fact: km, first registration, fuel, gearbox and the kind of car in sentence case ("Personenwagen, monovolume"; abbreviations like SUV stay as they are). The 2-column grid that left fuel alone on its own row is gone.
- **Stripes removed.** Actions and links are unchanged; the "Bekijken en bieden" button is at least 44px high.
- **Recently ended cards** follow the same layout: title without the year, the same facts, and "2 biedingen" with "afgelopen op 21/09/2026" beside it instead of "2 biedingen · veiling afgelopen"; the photo badge says "Afgelopen" (the date moved to the sentence).

The deadline wording lives in `ExportVehicle::offerDeadline()`, next to `windowHint` and `isBiddingOpen`. The facts are a partial shared by the two cards (`livewire/bidding-offer/_facts.blade.php`). New strings in nl, fr, en, de and es (`ui.bidding_through`, `ui.bidding_until_midnight`, `ui.bidding_ended_on`, `ui.bidding_bids`); the day counts reuse `ui.bidding_days_to_go` and `ui.bidding_last_day`.

Styles are Tailwind in the blade. The rules that only this card used (`.ui-card-auction*`, the bid grid override of `.ui-card-facts`, `.bod-afgelopen-melding`) are removed from refresh.css: 32 lines less, budget lowered in `tests/quality-ratchet.json`. The rules shared with the stocklist card (`.ui-card-eyebrow`, `.ui-card-dealer`, `.ui-stripes`) stay, because that card still uses them. No app-wide badge/facts components were on main when this started, so the styles stay local to this card.

### Business rules

R B1-2.9 described the "dagen" counter that turned amber at two days or less; it now describes the sentence, the last-day amber and what the card says, and when it changed. R B1-2.13 names the line on the recently ended cards.

### Tests

`TheBiddingCardReadsAtAGlanceTest` (`@rule B1-2.9`): days left with plurals (singular in nl, en, fr, de), the end day as "Laatste dag" and the only amber one (also at 23:50), a closed bidding as "Afgelopen op ...", the same number as `daysRemaining` before the end day, and the rendered card: "Nog 6 dagen", "tot en met 07/10/2026", "Personenwagen, monovolume", the year once, no middot, no spaced-capital label class, no stripes. Full suite and PHPStan pass locally.

Checked at 1440 (grid of three, cards in a row end on the same line) and 390 (no horizontal scroll).
params.title: The bidding card reads at a glance: the deadline in words, every fact once
